comments.author: bob
comments.body:
**Should fix** — single module-level `FILL_VALUE`

`fill.py` defines `FILL_VALUE = -9999.0` and `mask_fill` applies it to every column. The humidity column in the station CSVs uses `-999` and `n_samples` uses `-1`, so those sentinels survive into the means.

🤖 _AI-assisted comment, posted by @bob. AI assistance level: 5/5 (not read by a person)._

comments.author: erin
comments.body:
Agree — replaced `FILL_VALUE` with a `FILL_VALUES` dict keyed by column name, and `mask_fill` now takes the column.

🤖 _AI-assisted reply, posted by @erin. AI assistance level: 4/5 (read by a person, not edited)._

comments.author: bob
comments.body: Thanks. Worth saying plainly since it's bitten us twice: the sentinel is a property of the field, not of the file. Look it up per column every time.

comments.author: bob
comments.body:
**Should fix** — unknown column falls back to `-9999.0`

`FILL_VALUES.get(column, -9999.0)` silently applies the temperature sentinel to any column not in the table.
